note: PLACEHOLDER SAMPLE. Route concepts drawn from scratch — generic schematics, not traced from any broadcast or All-22 frame, which is what makes them yours (§2). Coordinates: x is 0–53.3 yards across the field, y is yards downfield from the line of scrimmage, negative behind it. `teams` tags which teams run the concept, and drives the by-team navigation.

data.name: Mesh
data.summary: Two shallow crossers run past each other a yard apart, forcing man defenders to navigate traffic and giving zone defenders two targets on the same plane.
data.beneficiaries: Quick separators and option-route slot receivers. Depresses aDOT, raises catch rate.

data.name: Dagger
data.summary: A seam route runs off the safety while a dig breaks underneath into the space it just vacated. The concept manufactures a throwing window rather than winning one.
data.beneficiaries: Big-slot receivers on the dig and vertical threats on the clear-out. Raises air yards share for the seam runner even without targets.

data.name: Sail
data.summary: Three routes attack one sideline at deep, intermediate, and flat depths, putting the flat defender in a bind he cannot solve without help.
data.beneficiaries: Tight ends and backs on the flat route, who see targets against soft coverage regardless of separation skill.
